translation.en: May 22
translation.kr: 5월 22일

raw: That the life of man is but a dream, many a man has surmised heretofore; and I, too, am everywhere pursued by this feeling. When I consider the narrow limits within which our active and inquiring faculties are confined; when I see how all our energies are wasted in providing for mere necessities, which again have no further end than to prolong a wretched existence; and then that all our satisfaction concerning certain subjects of investigation ends in nothing better than a passive resignation, whilst we amuse ourselves painting our prison-walls with bright figures and brilliant landscapes,—when I consider all this, Wilhelm, I am silent. I examine my own being, and find there a world, but a world rather of imagination and dim desires, than of distinctness and living power. Then everything swims before my senses, and I smile and dream while pursuing my way through the world.

translation.en: That a man's life is only a dream — many have guessed at that before me, and the feeling follows me everywhere too.
translation.kr: 사람의 삶이란 한낱 꿈에 지나지 않는다는 것 — 나보다 앞서 많은 이들이 그렇게 짐작했고, 그 느낌은 나에게도 어디서나 따라붙네.

translation.en: Consider how narrow the limits are that confine our active, inquiring powers.
translation.kr: 우리의 활동하고 탐구하는 힘을 가두는 한계가 얼마나 좁은지 생각해 보게.

translation.en: Consider how all our energy is spent providing for bare necessities, which in turn have no end beyond prolonging a wretched existence.
translation.kr: 우리의 온 기력이 겨우 먹고사는 일에 쓰이고, 그 일이란 또 비참한 목숨을 늘리는 것 말고는 아무 목적도 없다는 것을 생각해 보게.

translation.en: Consider how all our satisfaction on certain questions of enquiry comes to nothing better than a passive resignation, while we amuse ourselves painting our prison walls with bright figures and brilliant landscapes.
translation.kr: 어떤 탐구의 물음들에 대한 우리의 만족이라는 것도 결국 수동적인 체념밖에 되지 않는다는 것, 그러면서 우리는 감옥 벽에 밝은 형상과 화려한 풍경을 그려 넣으며 스스로를 달래고 있다는 것을 생각해 보게.

translation.en: When I consider all of it, Wilhelm, I fall silent.
translation.kr: 이 모든 것을 생각하면, 빌헬름, 나는 말문이 막히네.

translation.en: I examine my own being and find a world there — but a world of imagination and dim desire rather than of clear outline and living power.
translation.kr: 나 자신의 존재를 들여다보면 그 안에 하나의 세계가 있네. 그러나 뚜렷한 윤곽과 살아 있는 힘의 세계가 아니라, 상상과 어슴푸레한 욕망의 세계일세.

translation.en: Then everything swims before my senses, and I go on my way through the world smiling and dreaming.
translation.kr: 그러면 모든 것이 내 감각 앞에서 어른거리고, 나는 웃으며 꿈꾸며 세상을 걸어가네.

raw: All learned professors and doctors are agreed that children do not comprehend the cause of their desires; but that the grown-up should wander about this earth like children, without knowing whence they come, or whither they go, influenced as little by fixed motives, but guided like them by biscuits, sugar-plums, and the rod,—this is what nobody is willing to acknowledge; and yet I think it is palpable.

translation.en: All the learned professors and doctors agree that children do not understand the cause of their own desires.
translation.kr: 배운 교수와 박사들은 모두 아이들이 제 욕망의 까닭을 알지 못한다는 데 뜻을 같이하네.

translation.en: But that grown men should wander this earth like children, not knowing where they come from or where they are going, moved as little by settled motives, and steered just as children are by biscuits and sugar-plums and the rod — that is what nobody is willing to admit.
translation.kr: 그러나 다 자란 어른들도 아이처럼 이 땅을 헤매면서, 어디서 왔는지 어디로 가는지 알지 못하고, 확고한 동기에 움직이는 일도 그만큼 적으며, 아이들과 똑같이 과자와 사탕과 회초리에 끌려다닌다는 것 — 그것만은 아무도 인정하려 들지 않네.

translation.en: And yet I think it is plain enough.
translation.kr: 그런데도 내게는 그것이 너무나 분명해 보이네.

raw: I know what you will say in reply; for I am ready to admit that they are happiest, who, like children, amuse themselves with their playthings, dress and undress their dolls, and attentively watch the cupboard, where mamma has locked up her sweet things, and, when at last they get a delicious morsel, eat it greedily, and exclaim, "More!" These are certainly happy beings; but others also are objects of envy, who dignify their paltry employments, and sometimes even their passions, with pompous titles, representing them to mankind as gigantic achievements performed for their welfare and glory. But the man who humbly acknowledges the vanity of all this, who observes with what pleasure the thriving citizen converts his little garden into a paradise, and how patiently even the poor man pursues his weary way under his burden, and how all wish equally to behold the light of the sun a little longer,—yes, such a man is at peace, and creates his own world within himself; and he is also happy, because he is a man. And then, however limited his sphere, he still preserves in his bosom the sweet feeling of liberty, and knows that he can quit his prison whenever he likes.

translation.en: I know what you will say in reply, and I am ready to grant it: the happiest people are those who live like children.
translation.kr: 자네가 무어라 답할지 아네. 그리고 나도 인정할 준비가 되어 있네. 가장 행복한 사람은 아이처럼 사는 이들이라고.

translation.en: They amuse themselves with their playthings, dress and undress their dolls, and keep a careful watch on the cupboard where mother has locked up the sweet things.
translation.kr: 그들은 장난감을 가지고 놀고, 인형에게 옷을 입혔다 벗겼다 하고, 어머니가 단것을 넣어 잠가 둔 찬장을 눈여겨 지켜보지.

translation.en: And when they finally get a delicious mouthful, they eat it greedily and cry, "More!"
translation.kr: 그러다 마침내 맛있는 한 입을 얻으면 게걸스럽게 먹어 치우고는 "더!" 하고 외치네.

translation.en: They are certainly happy creatures.
translation.kr: 그들이 행복한 존재인 것은 틀림없네.

translation.en: But there are others to envy as well — those who dress up their paltry occupations, and sometimes even their passions, in grand titles, and present them to the world as gigantic achievements performed for its welfare and glory.
translation.kr: 그러나 부러워할 만한 이들은 또 있네. 보잘것없는 일거리, 때로는 제 욕정까지도 거창한 이름으로 치장하여, 세상의 복리와 영광을 위해 이룬 위대한 업적인 양 내놓는 자들 말일세.

translation.en: But then there is the man who humbly recognises how empty all this is.
translation.kr: 그러나 한편에는, 이 모든 것이 얼마나 헛된지를 겸허히 아는 사람도 있네.

translation.en: He sees with what pleasure the thriving townsman turns his little garden into a paradise, and how patiently even the poor man goes his weary way under his burden, and how all of them wish equally to see the light of the sun a little longer.
translation.kr: 그는 넉넉해진 시민이 제 작은 뜰을 낙원으로 가꾸며 얼마나 즐거워하는지, 가난한 사람조차 짐을 지고 고단한 길을 얼마나 참을성 있게 가는지, 그리고 그들 모두가 한결같이 햇빛을 조금이라도 더 보고 싶어 하는지를 보네.

translation.en: That man is at peace, and makes his own world within himself; and he too is happy, because he is a man.
translation.kr: 그런 사람은 평온하며, 제 안에 제 세계를 지어 올리네. 그리고 그 또한 행복한데, 사람이기 때문일세.

translation.en: And then, however narrow his sphere, he still keeps in his heart the sweet feeling of liberty, and knows he can leave this prison whenever he chooses.
translation.kr: 그리고 그 테두리가 아무리 좁아도, 그는 자유라는 달콤한 느낌을 가슴에 간직하고, 마음만 먹으면 언제든 이 감옥을 떠날 수 있다는 것을 아네.

translation.en: May 26
translation.kr: 5월 26일

raw: You know of old my ways of settling anywhere, of selecting a little cottage in some cosy spot, and of putting up in it with every inconvenience. Here, too, I have discovered such a snug, comfortable place, which possesses peculiar charms for me.

translation.en: You know my old way of settling anywhere — picking out a little cottage in some snug spot and putting up with every inconvenience in it.
translation.kr: 내가 어디든 자리 잡는 오랜 방식을 자네도 알지. 아늑한 곳에 작은 오두막을 하나 골라 놓고 온갖 불편을 그대로 견디는 것 말일세.

translation.en: Here too I have found such a comfortable place, one that holds a peculiar charm for me.
translation.kr: 여기서도 그런 편안한 자리를 하나 찾아냈네. 내게는 남다른 매력이 있는 곳이지.

raw: About a league from the town is a place called Walheim. (The reader need not take the trouble to look for the place thus designated. We have found it necessary to change the names given in the original.) It is delightfully situated on the side of a hill; and, by proceeding along one of the footpaths which lead out of the village, you can have a view of the whole valley. A good old woman lives there, who keeps a small inn. She sells wine, beer, and coffee, and is cheerful and pleasant notwithstanding her age. The chief charm of this spot consists in two linden-trees, spreading their enormous branches over the little green before the church, which is entirely surrounded by peasants' cottages, barns, and homesteads. I have seldom seen a place so retired and peaceable; and there often have my table and chair brought out from the little inn, and drink my coffee there, and read my Homer. Accident brought me to the spot one fine afternoon, and I found it perfectly deserted. Everybody was in the fields except a little boy about four years of age, who was sitting on the ground, and held between his knees a child about six months old: he pressed it to his bosom with both arms, which thus formed a sort of arm-chair; and, notwithstanding the liveliness which sparkled in its black eyes, it remained perfectly still. The sight charmed me. I sat down upon a plough opposite, and sketched with great delight this little picture of brotherly tenderness. I added the neighbouring hedge, the barn-door, and some broken cart-wheels, just as they happened to lie; and I found in about an hour that I had made a very correct and interesting drawing, without putting in the slightest thing of my own. This confirmed me in my resolution of adhering, for the future, entirely to nature. She alone is inexhaustible, and capable of forming the greatest masters. Much may be alleged in favour of rules, as much may be likewise advanced in favour of the laws of society: an artist formed upon them will never produce anything absolutely bad or disgusting; as a man who observes the laws, and obeys decorum, can never be an absolutely intolerable neighbour, nor a decided villain: but yet, say what you will of rules, they destroy the genuine feeling of nature, as well as its true expression. Do not tell me "that this is too hard, that they only restrain and prune superfluous branches, etc." My good friend, I will illustrate this by an analogy. These things resemble love. A warmhearted youth becomes strongly attached to a maiden: he spends every hour of the day in her company, wears out his health, and lavishes his fortune, to afford continual proof that he is wholly devoted to her. Then comes a man of the world, a man of place and respectability, and addresses him thus: "My good young friend, love is natural; but you must love within bounds. Divide your time: devote a portion to business, and give the hours of recreation to your mistress. Calculate your fortune; and out of the superfluity you may make her a present, only not too often,—on her birthday, and such occasions." Pursuing this advice, he may become a useful member of society, and I should advise every prince to give him an appointment; but it is all up with his love, and with his genius if he be an artist. O my friend! why is it that the torrent of genius so seldom bursts forth, so seldom rolls in full-flowing stream, overwhelming your astounded soul? Because, on either side of this stream, cold and respectable persons have taken up their abodes, and, forsooth, their summer-houses and tulip-beds would suffer from the torrent; wherefore they dig trenches, and raise embankments betimes, in order to avert the impending danger.

translation.en: About a league from the town is a place called Walheim.
translation.kr: 마을에서 십 리쯤 되는 곳에 발하임이라는 데가 있네.

translation.en: (The reader need not go to the trouble of looking for it: we have found it necessary to change the names given in the original.)
translation.kr: (독자는 굳이 그곳을 찾아보려 애쓸 것 없다. 원고에 적힌 이름들은 바꿀 수밖에 없었다.)

translation.en: It lies beautifully on the side of a hill, and if you follow one of the footpaths out of the village you can look out over the whole valley.
translation.kr: 언덕 비탈에 아름답게 자리 잡고 있어서, 마을을 벗어나는 오솔길 하나를 따라가면 골짜기 전체를 내려다볼 수 있네.

translation.en: A good old woman lives there who keeps a small inn.
translation.kr: 그곳에는 작은 주막을 치는 마음씨 좋은 노파가 사네.

translation.en: She sells wine, beer, and coffee, and for all her age she is cheerful and pleasant.
translation.kr: 포도주와 맥주와 커피를 파는데, 나이가 그만큼 들었는데도 밝고 상냥하네.

translation.en: The great charm of the place is two linden-trees, spreading their enormous branches over the little green in front of the church, which is ringed about with peasants' cottages, barns, and farmyards.
translation.kr: 이곳의 가장 큰 매력은 보리수 두 그루일세. 교회 앞 작은 잔디밭 위로 거대한 가지를 펼치고 있고, 그 둘레에는 농가와 헛간과 마당이 둘러 있지.

translation.en: I have seldom seen a spot so quiet and so much its own.
translation.kr: 이토록 고요하고 제 빛깔이 오롯한 곳은 좀처럼 본 적이 없네.

translation.en: I often have my table and chair carried out from the little inn, and drink my coffee there and read my Homer.
translation.kr: 나는 자주 작은 주막에서 탁자와 의자를 내오게 하여, 거기서 커피를 마시며 내 호메로스를 읽네.

translation.en: Chance brought me there one fine afternoon, and I found the place completely deserted.
translation.kr: 어느 맑은 오후 우연히 그곳에 갔다가, 마을이 텅 비어 있는 것을 보았네.

translation.en: Everyone was in the fields except a little boy of about four, who sat on the ground holding a baby of six months between his knees.
translation.kr: 다들 들에 나가고 없었는데, 네 살쯤 된 사내아이 하나만 땅바닥에 앉아 여섯 달쯤 된 아기를 무릎 사이에 안고 있더군.

translation.en: He pressed it to his chest with both arms, so that he made a kind of armchair for it; and for all the liveliness sparkling in its black eyes, the baby stayed perfectly still.
translation.kr: 두 팔로 아기를 가슴에 꼭 끌어안아 마치 팔걸이의자를 만들어 준 것 같았네. 아기는 검은 눈에 생기가 반짝이면서도 조금도 움직이지 않았지.

translation.en: The sight delighted me.
translation.kr: 그 광경이 나를 기쁘게 했네.

translation.en: I sat down on a plough opposite them and sketched this little picture of brotherly tenderness with great pleasure.
translation.kr: 나는 맞은편 쟁기에 앉아 이 형제애의 작은 그림을 아주 즐겁게 그렸네.

translation.en: I added the hedge nearby, the barn door, and some broken cart-wheels, just as they happened to lie.
translation.kr: 가까이 있던 울타리와 헛간 문, 그리고 부서진 수레바퀴 몇 개를 놓여 있는 그대로 보태어 넣었지.

translation.en: After about an hour I found I had made a drawing that was accurate and full of interest, without having put in the slightest thing of my own.
translation.kr: 한 시간쯤 지나고 보니, 내 것이라고는 티끌만큼도 보태지 않고도 정확하고 흥미로운 그림 한 장이 되어 있더군.

translation.en: That confirmed me in my resolve to hold, from now on, entirely to nature.
translation.kr: 그 일로 나는 앞으로는 오로지 자연에 충실하겠다는 결심을 굳혔네.

translation.en: She alone is inexhaustible, and she alone can form a great master.
translation.kr: 오직 자연만이 다함이 없고, 오직 자연만이 위대한 대가를 길러 낼 수 있네.

translation.en: Much can be said for rules, just as much can be said for the laws of society.
translation.kr: 규칙을 두고 할 말이 많다는 것은, 사회의 법을 두고 할 말이 많은 것과 마찬가지일세.

translation.en: An artist trained on them will never produce anything downright bad or disgusting, just as a man who keeps the law and observes decorum can never be a wholly intolerable neighbour or an outright villain.
translation.kr: 규칙으로 다듬어진 예술가가 아주 나쁘거나 역겨운 것을 내놓는 일은 결코 없네. 법을 지키고 예절을 따르는 사람이 도저히 못 견딜 이웃이나 노골적인 악당이 될 수 없는 것과 같지.

translation.en: But say what you like about rules: they destroy the genuine feeling of nature, and its true expression with it.
translation.kr: 그러나 규칙에 대해 무어라 하든, 규칙은 자연의 참된 감정을 죽이고 그 참된 표현까지 함께 죽이네.

translation.en: Do not tell me that this is too hard, that rules only restrain and prune away superfluous branches, etc.
translation.kr: 그것이 너무 심한 말이라거니, 규칙은 그저 웃자란 가지를 억제하고 쳐 낼 뿐이라거니 하는 말은 하지 말게.

translation.en: My good friend, let me put it to you by way of a comparison.
translation.kr: 친구여, 비유를 들어 말해 보겠네.

translation.en: These things are like love.
translation.kr: 이런 것은 사랑과 같네.

translation.en: A warm-hearted young man attaches himself deeply to a girl.
translation.kr: 마음이 뜨거운 젊은이가 한 처녀에게 깊이 빠졌다고 하세.

translation.en: He spends every hour of the day in her company, wears out his health, and squanders his fortune, all to prove at every moment that he is wholly hers.
translation.kr: 그는 온종일 모든 시간을 그 여자 곁에서 보내고, 건강을 축내고, 재산을 탕진하네. 자기가 온전히 그 여자의 것임을 순간마다 증명하려고 말일세.

translation.en: Then along comes a man of the world, a man of position and respectability, who says to him: "My good young friend, love is natural; but you must love within bounds.
translation.kr: 그때 세상 물정에 밝은 사람, 지위 있고 존경받는 사람이 나타나 이렇게 말하네. "이보게 젊은이, 사랑은 자연스러운 것이네. 그러나 분수에 맞게 사랑해야 하네."

translation.en: Divide your time: give a part of it to business, and keep your hours of recreation for your mistress.
translation.kr: "시간을 나누게. 얼마는 일에 쓰고, 여가 시간은 애인에게 두게."

translation.en: Reckon up your fortune, and out of what is left over you may make her a present — only not too often; on her birthday, and such occasions."
translation.kr: "재산을 헤아려 보고, 남는 것으로 선물을 해 주게. 다만 너무 자주는 말고, 생일이라든가 그런 때에만 말일세."

translation.en: If he follows this advice, he may turn into a useful member of society, and I would advise any prince to give him a post.
translation.kr: 이 충고를 따르면 그는 사회에 쓸모 있는 일원이 될 것이고, 나라도 어느 제후에게든 그에게 자리를 주라고 권하겠네.

translation.en: But it is all over with his love — and with his genius, if he is an artist.
translation.kr: 그러나 그의 사랑은 끝장이 났네. 예술가라면 그의 천재도 함께 끝장이 났고.

translation.en: Oh, my friend! Why is it that the torrent of genius so seldom bursts out, so seldom comes rolling down in full flood to overwhelm your astonished soul?
translation.kr: 아, 친구여! 어찌하여 천재의 격류는 그토록 드물게만 터져 나오고, 그토록 드물게만 넘쳐흘러 놀란 영혼을 휩쓸어 가는가?

translation.en: Because on both banks of that stream live cool and respectable people, whose summer-houses and tulip-beds would suffer from a flood.
translation.kr: 그 물길 양쪽 기슭에 점잖고 냉정한 사람들이 살고 있기 때문일세. 물이 넘치면 그들의 정자와 튤립 화단이 상하고 말 테니까.

translation.en: So they dig their trenches and raise their embankments in good time, to head off the danger before it comes.
translation.kr: 그래서 그들은 미리 도랑을 파고 둑을 쌓아, 위험이 닥치기 전에 막아 버리는 것이지.

translation.en: May 27
translation.kr: 5월 27일

raw: I find I have fallen into raptures, declamation, and similes, and have forgotten, in consequence, to tell you what became of the children. Absorbed in my artistic contemplations, which I briefly described in my letter of yesterday, I continued sitting on the plough for two hours. Toward evening a young woman, with a basket on her arm, came running toward the children, who had not moved all that time. She exclaimed from a distance, "You are a good boy, Philip!" She gave me greeting: I returned it, rose, and approached her. I inquired if she were the mother of those pretty children. "Yes," she said; and, giving the eldest a piece of bread, she took the little one in her arms and kissed it with a mother's tenderness. "I left my child in Philip's care," she said, "whilst I went into the town with my eldest boy to buy some wheaten bread, some sugar, and an earthen pot." I saw the various articles in the basket, from which the cover had fallen. "I shall make some broth to-night for my little Hans (which was the name of the youngest): that wild fellow, the big one, broke my pot yesterday, whilst he was scrambling with Philip for what remained of the contents." I inquired for the eldest; and she had scarcely time to tell me that he was driving a couple of geese home from the meadow, when he ran up, and handed Philip an osier-twig. I talked a little longer with the woman, and found that she was the daughter of the schoolmaster, and that her husband was gone on a journey into Switzerland for some money a relation had left him. "They wanted to cheat him," she said, "and would not answer his letters; so he is gone there himself. I hope he has met with no accident, as I have heard nothing of him since his departure." I left the woman, with regret, giving each of the children a kreutzer, with an additional one for the youngest, to buy some wheaten bread for his broth when she went to town next; and so we parted. I assure you, my dear friend, when my thoughts are all in tumult, the sight of such a creature as this tranquillises my disturbed mind. She moves in a happy thoughtlessness within the confined circle of her existence; she supplies her wants from day to day; and, when she sees the leaves fall, they raise no other idea in her mind than that winter is approaching. Since that time I have gone out there frequently. The children have become quite familiar with me; and each gets a lump of sugar when I drink my coffee, and they share my milk and bread and butter in the evening. They always receive their kreutzer on Sundays, for the good woman has orders to give it to them when I do not go there after evening service. They are quite at home with me, tell me everything; and I am particularly amused with observing their tempers, and the simplicity of their behaviour, when some of the other village children are assembled with them.

translation.en: I find I have fallen into raptures and declamation and similes, and so forgotten to tell you what became of the children.
translation.kr: 돌아보니 내가 감격과 열변과 비유에 빠져, 그 아이들이 어떻게 되었는지 자네에게 말하는 것을 잊고 말았군.

translation.en: Absorbed in the artistic contemplations I sketched for you in yesterday's letter, I went on sitting on that plough for two hours.
translation.kr: 어제 편지에 적어 보낸 그 예술적 명상에 잠긴 채, 나는 그 쟁기 위에 두 시간이나 앉아 있었네.

translation.en: Toward evening a young woman came running toward the children with a basket on her arm.
translation.kr: 저녁 무렵 젊은 아낙이 팔에 바구니를 끼고 아이들 쪽으로 달려왔네.

translation.en: They had not moved the whole time.
translation.kr: 아이들은 그동안 내내 꼼짝도 하지 않았지.

translation.en: She called out while she was still some way off, "You are a good boy, Philip!"
translation.kr: 그 여자는 아직 멀리서부터 소리쳤네. "착하기도 하지, 필립!"

translation.en: She greeted me; I returned it, got up, and went over to her.
translation.kr: 그러고는 내게 인사를 했네. 나도 인사를 받고 일어나 그쪽으로 갔지.

translation.en: I asked whether she was the mother of those pretty children.
translation.kr: 저 예쁜 아이들의 어머니냐고 물었네.

translation.en: "Yes," she said; and giving the eldest a piece of bread, she took the baby in her arms and kissed it with a mother's tenderness.
translation.kr: "그렇습니다" 하고 말하고는, 큰아이에게 빵 한 조각을 쥐여 주고 아기를 팔에 안아 어머니다운 다정함으로 입을 맞추더군.

translation.en: "I left my child in Philip's care," she said, "while I went into town with my eldest boy to buy some wheat bread, some sugar, and an earthen pot."
translation.kr: "큰아이를 데리고 마을에 밀빵이랑 설탕이랑 질그릇을 사러 가느라, 아기는 필립에게 맡겨 두었지요" 하고 그 여자가 말했네.

translation.en: I could see the various things in the basket; the cover had slipped off.
translation.kr: 바구니 덮개가 벗겨져 있어서 안에 든 것들이 보였네.

translation.en: "I am going to make some broth tonight for my little Hans," she said.
translation.kr: "오늘 저녁에는 우리 한스에게 죽을 쑤어 줄 참이에요" 하고 그 여자가 말했네.

translation.en: "That wild fellow, the big one, broke my pot yesterday, scrambling with Philip over what was left in it."
translation.kr: "저 큰 녀석, 저 말썽꾸러기가 어제 필립이랑 남은 것을 두고 다투다가 제 냄비를 깨뜨려 버렸지 뭐예요."

translation.en: I asked after the eldest, and she had hardly had time to tell me he was driving a couple of geese home from the meadow when he came running up and handed Philip a willow switch.
translation.kr: 큰아이는 어디 갔느냐고 묻자, 초원에서 거위 두어 마리를 몰고 오는 중이라고 채 대답하기도 전에 그 아이가 달려와 필립에게 버들가지 하나를 건네주었네.

translation.en: I talked a little longer with the woman and learned that she was the schoolmaster's daughter, and that her husband had gone off to Switzerland to collect some money a relative had left him.
translation.kr: 그 여자와 좀 더 이야기를 나누다가, 그가 학교 선생의 딸이며, 남편은 친척이 남긴 돈을 받으러 스위스에 갔다는 것을 알게 되었네.

translation.en: "They meant to cheat him," she said, "and would not answer his letters, so he has gone there himself.
translation.kr: "사람들이 남편을 속이려 들었대요" 하고 그 여자가 말했네. "편지에 답도 하지 않기에 직접 간 것이지요."

translation.en: I hope nothing has happened to him; I have heard nothing since he left."
translation.kr: "별일 없어야 할 텐데요. 떠난 뒤로는 아무 소식도 없어요."

translation.en: I was sorry to leave the woman.
translation.kr: 그 여자와 헤어지기가 서운했네.

translation.en: I gave each of the children a kreutzer, and one more for the youngest, to buy him some wheat bread for his broth the next time she went to town; and so we parted.
translation.kr: 아이들에게 크로이처를 한 닢씩 주고, 막내 몫으로 한 닢을 더 주었네. 다음에 마을에 나갈 때 죽에 넣을 밀빵을 사 오라고 말일세. 그렇게 우리는 헤어졌네.

translation.en: I tell you, my dear friend, when my thoughts are all in turmoil, the sight of a creature like this settles my troubled mind.
translation.kr: 정말이지 친구여, 내 생각이 온통 뒤엉킬 때면, 이런 사람의 모습이 어지러운 내 마음을 가라앉혀 주네.

translation.en: She moves in a happy thoughtlessness inside the narrow circle of her life, supplying her wants from one day to the next.
translation.kr: 그 여자는 제 삶의 좁은 테두리 안에서 행복한 무심함으로 움직이며, 하루하루 필요한 것을 마련해 가네.

translation.en: And when she sees the leaves falling, it raises no thought in her but that winter is coming.
translation.kr: 그리고 잎이 떨어지는 것을 보아도, 겨울이 오는구나 하는 생각 말고는 아무 생각도 일지 않지.

translation.en: Since then I have gone out there often.
translation.kr: 그 뒤로 나는 자주 그곳에 나가네.

translation.en: The children are quite used to me now.
translation.kr: 아이들은 이제 나와 아주 스스럼이 없네.

translation.en: Each of them gets a lump of sugar when I drink my coffee, and in the evening they share my bread and butter and milk.
translation.kr: 내가 커피를 마실 때면 저마다 각설탕을 하나씩 얻고, 저녁이면 내 버터 바른 빵과 우유를 나누어 먹지.

translation.en: They always get their kreutzer on Sundays, since the good woman has orders to give it to them whenever I am not there after evening service.
translation.kr: 일요일마다 크로이처를 꼭 받는데, 저녁 예배가 끝난 뒤 내가 없을 때는 그 마음씨 좋은 아낙이 대신 주도록 일러 두었기 때문일세.

translation.en: They are entirely at home with me and tell me everything.
translation.kr: 아이들은 내게 아주 마음을 놓고 무엇이든 다 이야기하네.

translation.en: I am particularly amused by their tempers, and by how simply they behave when some of the other village children are gathered with them.
translation.kr: 특히 재미있는 것은 마을의 다른 아이들이 함께 모였을 때 드러나는 그 성미와 꾸밈없는 몸가짐일세.

raw: It has given me a deal of trouble to satisfy the anxiety of the mother, lest (as she says) "they should inconvenience the gentleman."

translation.en: It has cost me a good deal of trouble to quiet the mother's anxiety.
translation.kr: 그 어머니의 걱정을 가라앉히느라 적잖이 애를 먹었네.

translation.en: She is afraid, as she puts it, that "they should inconvenience the gentleman."
translation.kr: 그 여자 말로는 "아이들이 나리께 폐가 될까" 두렵다는 것일세.

translation.en: May 30
translation.kr: 5월 30일

raw: What I have lately said of painting is equally true with respect to poetry. It is only necessary for us to know what is really excellent, and venture to give it expression; and that is saying much in few words. To-day I have had a scene, which, if literally related, would, make the most beautiful idyl in the world. But why should I talk of poetry and scenes and idyls? Can we never take pleasure in nature without having recourse to art?

translation.en: What I said lately about painting holds just as true of poetry.
translation.kr: 요전에 그림에 대해 한 말은 시에도 똑같이 들어맞네.

translation.en: All we need is to recognise what is really excellent, and to dare to give it expression — and that is a great deal said in few words.
translation.kr: 우리에게 필요한 것은 참으로 빼어난 것을 알아보는 일, 그리고 그것을 감히 말로 옮기는 일뿐일세. 짧은 말에 많은 것을 담은 셈이지.

translation.en: Today I had a scene which, set down just as it happened, would make the most beautiful idyll in the world.
translation.kr: 오늘 겪은 일을 있는 그대로 옮겨 적기만 해도, 세상에서 가장 아름다운 목가가 될 걸세.

translation.en: But why talk of poetry and scenes and idylls?
translation.kr: 그러나 시니 장면이니 목가니 하는 말은 무엇 하러 하는가?

translation.en: Can we never take pleasure in nature without having to fall back on art?
translation.kr: 우리는 예술에 기대지 않고는 자연을 즐길 수 없단 말인가?

raw: If you expect anything grand or magnificent from this introduction, you will be sadly mistaken. It relates merely to a peasant-lad, who has excited in me the warmest interest. As usual, I shall tell my story badly; and you, as usual, will think me extravagant. It is Walheim once more—always Walheim—which produces these wonderful phenomena.

translation.en: If you are expecting anything grand or magnificent after that introduction, you will be badly disappointed.
translation.kr: 이렇게 운을 떼었으니 무슨 거창하고 웅장한 이야기를 기대한다면, 자네는 크게 실망할 걸세.

translation.en: It concerns nothing more than a peasant lad who has stirred the warmest interest in me.
translation.kr: 그저 내 마음을 더없이 뜨겁게 끈 한 시골 총각에 관한 이야기일 뿐이네.

translation.en: As usual I shall tell the story badly, and as usual you will think me extravagant.
translation.kr: 늘 그렇듯 나는 이야기를 서툴게 할 것이고, 늘 그렇듯 자네는 나를 과장이 심하다 여기겠지.

translation.en: It is Walheim again — always Walheim — that produces these wonders.
translation.kr: 이런 놀라운 일들을 빚어내는 것은 또 발하임일세. 언제나 발하임이지.

raw: A party had assembled outside the house under the linden-trees, to drink coffee. The company did not exactly please me; and, under one pretext or another, I lingered behind.

translation.en: A party had gathered outside the house under the linden-trees to drink coffee.
translation.kr: 보리수 아래 집 앞에 사람들이 모여 커피를 마시고 있었네.

translation.en: The company did not quite suit me, and on one pretext or another I hung back.
translation.kr: 그 자리가 썩 마음에 들지 않아, 이런저런 핑계를 대고 나는 뒤에 처져 있었지.

raw: A peasant came from an adjoining house, and set to work arranging some part of the same plough which I had lately sketched. His appearance pleased me; and I spoke to him, inquired about his circumstances, made his acquaintance, and, as is my wont with persons of that class, was soon admitted into his confidence. He said he was in the service of a young widow, who set great store by him. He spoke so much of his mistress, and praised her so extravagantly, that I could soon see he was desperately in love with her. "She is no longer young," he said: "and she was treated so badly by her former husband that she does not mean to marry again." From his account it was so evident what incomparable charms she possessed for him, and how ardently he wished she would select him to extinguish the recollection of her first husband's misconduct, that I should have to repeat his own words in order to describe the depth of the poor fellow's attachment, truth, and devotion. It would, in fact, require the gifts of a great poet to convey the expression of his features, the harmony of his voice, and the heavenly fire of his eye. No words can portray the tenderness of his every movement and of every feature: no effort of mine could do justice to the scene. His alarm lest I should misconceive his position with regard to his mistress, or question the propriety of her conduct, touched me particularly. The charming manner with which he described her form and person, which, without possessing the graces of youth, won and attached him to her, is inexpressible, and must be left to the imagination. I have never in my life witnessed or fancied or conceived the possibility of such intense devotion, such ardent affections, united with so much purity. Do not blame me if I say that the recollection of this innocence and truth is deeply impressed upon my very soul; that this picture of fidelity and tenderness haunts me everywhere; and that my own heart, as though enkindled by the flame, glows and burns within me.

translation.en: A peasant came out of a house nearby and set to work on part of the same plough I had sketched not long before.
translation.kr: 가까운 집에서 농부 하나가 나오더니, 얼마 전 내가 그렸던 바로 그 쟁기의 한 부분을 손보기 시작했네.

translation.en: I liked the look of him.
translation.kr: 그 사람의 생김새가 마음에 들었네.

translation.en: I spoke to him, asked about his circumstances, made his acquaintance, and — as usually happens between me and people of that class — was soon taken into his confidence.
translation.kr: 말을 붙여 사정을 묻고 서로 알게 되었는데, 나와 그런 계층의 사람들 사이에 흔히 그렇듯 이내 속내를 털어놓더군.

translation.en: He told me he was in the service of a young widow who thought highly of him.
translation.kr: 그는 자기를 아주 좋게 보아 주는 젊은 과부 집에서 일한다고 했네.

translation.en: He spoke so much about his mistress, and praised her so extravagantly, that I could soon see he was desperately in love with her.
translation.kr: 제 여주인 이야기를 어찌나 많이 하고 어찌나 침이 마르게 칭찬하는지, 그가 그 여자를 애타게 사랑하고 있다는 것을 이내 알 수 있었네.

translation.en: "She is no longer young," he said.
translation.kr: "이제 젊지는 않으십니다" 하고 그가 말했네.

translation.en: "She was treated so badly by her first husband that she does not mean to marry again."
translation.kr: "첫 남편에게 하도 모질게 당하셔서 다시는 시집갈 생각이 없으시답니다."

translation.en: From the way he spoke it was plain what incomparable charms she had for him.
translation.kr: 말하는 품으로 보아, 그 여자가 그에게 얼마나 견줄 데 없는 매력을 지닌 사람인지는 분명했네.

translation.en: It was plain how fiercely he wished she would choose him, and wipe out the memory of her first husband's misconduct.
translation.kr: 그리고 그 여자가 자기를 골라 주어 첫 남편의 못된 짓에 대한 기억을 지워 주기를 그가 얼마나 간절히 바라는지도 분명했지.

translation.en: To convey the depth of the poor fellow's attachment, his truthfulness and devotion, I would have to repeat his own words.
translation.kr: 이 가엾은 사내의 애착과 진실함과 헌신이 얼마나 깊은지를 전하려면, 그의 말을 그대로 옮기는 수밖에 없을 걸세.

translation.en: It would take a great poet to render the look on his face, the harmony of his voice, the heavenly fire in his eye.
translation.kr: 그 얼굴빛, 그 목소리의 가락, 그 눈에 어린 천상의 불길을 옮기려면 위대한 시인이라야 하겠지.

translation.en: No words of mine can catch the tenderness of his every movement and every expression; no effort of mine could do the scene justice.
translation.kr: 그 몸짓 하나하나, 표정 하나하나에 담긴 다정함을 내 말로는 담아낼 수 없네. 내 아무리 애써도 그 장면을 제대로 그려 낼 수는 없을 걸세.

translation.en: What touched me most was his fear that I might misunderstand his position with regard to his mistress, or doubt the propriety of her conduct.
translation.kr: 무엇보다 나를 울린 것은, 내가 여주인에 대한 제 처지를 오해하거나 그 여자의 행실을 의심할까 봐 그가 두려워하는 마음이었네.

translation.en: The charm with which he described her figure and her person — which, without the graces of youth, had taken hold of him and bound him to her — cannot be put into words, and must be left to the imagination.
translation.kr: 젊음의 고운 태는 없으면서도 그를 사로잡아 붙들어 맨 그 여자의 몸매와 자태를 그리는 그 정겨움은, 말로는 옮길 수 없고 상상에 맡길 수밖에 없네.

translation.en: Never in my life have I witnessed, or imagined, or thought possible, such intense devotion, such ardent affection, joined with so much purity.
translation.kr: 그토록 깊은 헌신과 그토록 뜨거운 애정이 그토록 순수함과 하나가 된 것을, 나는 평생 본 적도 상상한 적도, 있을 수 있다고 여긴 적조차 없네.

translation.en: Do not blame me if I say that the memory of this innocence and truth is stamped deep into my soul.
translation.kr: 이 순진함과 진실함의 기억이 내 영혼에 깊이 새겨졌다고 말해도 나를 나무라지 말게.

translation.en: This picture of fidelity and tenderness follows me everywhere.
translation.kr: 이 성실과 다정함의 그림이 어디를 가나 나를 따라다니네.

translation.en: And my own heart, as though kindled at that flame, glows and burns within me.
translation.kr: 그리고 내 마음도 그 불길에 붙은 듯 안에서 달아오르고 타오르네.

raw: I mean now to try and see her as soon as I can: or perhaps, on second thoughts, I had better not; it is better I should behold her through the eyes of her lover. To my sight, perhaps, she would not appear as she now stands before me; and why should I destroy so sweet a picture?

translation.en: I mean to try to see her as soon as I can.
translation.kr: 되도록 빨리 그 여자를 한번 보아야겠다고 생각하네.

translation.en: Or perhaps, on second thoughts, I had better not: better that I should see her through her lover's eyes.
translation.kr: 아니, 다시 생각하니 그러지 않는 편이 낫겠네. 그 남자의 눈을 통해 보는 편이 나을 걸세.

translation.en: Seen with my own, she might not appear as she now stands before me — and why should I spoil so sweet a picture?
translation.kr: 내 눈으로 보면 지금 내 앞에 서 있는 그 모습과 다를지도 모르니 — 그 고운 그림을 무엇 하러 망가뜨리겠나?
